title: Terrain ruggedness for mountain lion habitat suitability
method: Terrain Ruggedness Index as defined in the task: per cell, root-mean-square of the elevation differences to the 8 neighbours (Riley-type TRI), NoData from the alpha band excluded; mapped as a continuous raster.

key_parameters.units: grey levels of the 8-bit elevation export (relative)

benchmark_defects: Elevation.tif is a 4-band 8-bit RGBA rendering (grey 0-255 + alpha), not a DEM in metres; TRI is therefore only relative and cannot be interpreted in metres.

In the published reference script the plotting and savefig lines follow a `return` statement inside a separate function, `rescale_by_function`, which main() does not call; main() computes the filter and writes no file.
The published reference script computes the 3x3 range (max-min), which differs from the TRI definition given in the Domain Knowledge.
checks: required: a captured DEM-shaped 2-D array is a TRI-family surface: Spearman >= 0.95 against the gold TRI (1/4 grid) or, for coarser arrays, against the TRI recomputed from the gold DEM decimated to that grid (slope 0.93 fails)

required: the figure shows the ruggedness surface (>= 0.95) in either vertical orientation: imshow by origin, pcolormesh by index-space y direction (coordinate space: both vertical orientations), contour/contourf via the Z argument of the plotting call checked against the contour levels; otherwise UNVERIFIABLE (not passed); transposes / left-right mirrors fail
figure (kind=figure, not in the main metric): the surface is drawn north-up (check above in the orientation drawn)
